subject: 2012 bin files - will only analyse one file at a time (g.part2)

messages.author: 0ba6fa6f78e733b5
messages.subject: 2012 bin files - will only analyse one file at a time (g.part2)
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I'm trying to analyse some old bin files (GENEActiv 2012) with the latest GGIR (only parts 1 and 2). The meta files were all created, but only one ms.2 file was initially created and the error message was:

Part 2
 1 2Error in matrix(" ", 1, (ncol(SUMMARY) - ncol(SUM$summary))) :
  invalid 'ncol' value (< 0)

By re-running it I can get the extra ms.2 files, but then I get the same error message and no part 2 summary files are created. The pdf of the graphs in QC only shows two graphs (there are 57 files).

I have tried removing files and running one at a time. It seems to work fine on any file individually, but then trips up as soon as there is more than one.

The same code works fine on other folders of files. The data were collect at 87.5 Hz for 7 days and started at midnight. The files had no ID added and I have tried renaming them with an ID added upfront - again it will only analyse one at a time. I have also tried Idloc as 1 and 2.

Any thoughts/suggestions would be much appreciated.

I have attached one meta file FYI. If another would be helpful let me know, I can only attach one in a post.

Thanks,
Alex

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] 2012 bin files - will only analyse one file at a time (g.part2)
parts:
Hi Alex,

To fix this please rename the first data file in your data folder such that it is not alphabetically the first anymore, e.g. by adding a z at the beginning of the filename. Next, make sure you delete any milestone data related to its previous filename and then reprocess the file for all parts of the analyses.

If you notice that the file size is very small, e.g. only a few kilobytes, then take it out of your data folder, because it would be empty anyway.

Explanation:
GGIR uses the variable names generated for the first file in a dataset as a reference for merging the results from all other files. If, for whatever reason, the first file is not considered valid then it will not have a full variable list for that file and other datafiles will struggle to merge with it. This is a bug I have been aware of for a while, but have not had time yet to fix. Note that this does not affect the analyses, but only causes the processing to stop when you encounter a healthy normal file. That then gives the misleading impression that something is wrong with that healthy file. Removing respective milestone files will not address the problem, because GGIR will continue to use the problematic first file as a reference. The fix I describe above should address the issue because it will ensure that another file is used as a reference.

The data format should have remained unchanged since GENEActiv was first introduced, so I have no reason to believe that year of measurement plays a role.

Vincent
